current_answer: Current evidence supports several distinct routes: fal H3 Max Director is a finite hosted context-carrying WebRTC session; Yoroll says H3 Superfast powers YoLive, a group proposal-and-vote route; Reactor FastH3 is a high-end queue-and-playout route; FastVideo documents local FastH3 clip paths and a four-GPU Dreamverse frame-carried Preview v1 profile; a community project reports one RTX 5090 sustaining a retimed dense FastH3 channel; Comfy offers local H3 paths; and vLLM-Omni documents a separate H3 service. vLLM-Omni’s current H3 recipe says step execution can admit requests between denoise steps, but its stated two-H100 test found four simultaneous H3 jobs slower under four-way co-batching than ordinary request mode. Its documented two-RTX-5090 DLO launch selects the FL2VA task path, which serves T2VA and FL2VA, and recommends a 384 GiB host; its one 50-step T2VA validation returned about 5.17 seconds of output in 8 minutes 38 seconds. Treat task path, client capability, arrival pattern, and a recorded output as separate facts. No cited H3 result establishes a live viewer experience.

catalogue_card.question: Does H3 continuous batching make a four-request queue faster?
catalogue_card.text: Not in vLLM-Omni’s published two-H100 test. Four simultaneous H3 jobs took longer with four-way co-batching than in ordinary request mode. It is a queue boundary, not a live-video result.

summary: vLLM-Omni says H3 can admit and retire requests between denoise steps, but its stated two-H100 test with four simultaneous 672×384, 209-frame, 30-step requests reports worse wall time and mean latency under four-way co-batching than ordinary request mode.
The source says staggered-arrival behavior remains unmeasured. The benchmark does not predict two RTX 5090 GPUs, a different job shape, a FastH3 adapter, a browser-visible result, or a public stream.

The current two-RTX-5090 DLO launch selects the FL2VA DiT; T2VA uses that path. The source recommends a 384 GiB host, while its one 50-step T2VA validation returned 124 1344×768 / 24 fps frames in 8 minutes 38 seconds.
vLLM-Omni’s current ComfyUI client still accepts one FL2VA frame even though the server recipe can represent ordered first-and-last-frame inputs.
uncertainty: The batching result is one project-maintained two-H100 benchmark with four simultaneous requests. Staggered arrivals, other job shapes, other hardware, and viewer-visible behavior remain unmeasured.
The documented two-RTX-5090 result is one project-published T2VA validation. The pool did not independently audit its environment, media, timing, or quality.

The two-5090 command selects the FL2VA path; it does not establish a combined multi-task service, Ref2VA, a two-keyframe client workflow, warm performance, streaming, queueing, or first visible frame.
vLLM-Omni’s current ComfyUI client-scope statements come from an open RFC. The pool did not install or test the server or client.
Dreamverse’s FastH3 profile is project documentation; the pool did not install or run it, inspect a generated handoff, or measure buffer, cost, recovery, or uptime.
FastVideo and ComfyUI still conflict on FastH3 8-Step V2 FL2VA scope. The pool did not run a pinned T2VA or FL2VA workflow.
No pool test, invoice, uptime log, end-to-end source-to-visible latency measurement, or first-party pool analytics record is available.
freshness_note: Checked 26 September 2026. The new evidence is a named vLLM-Omni H3 batching benchmark: four simultaneous requests did not gain throughput from four-way co-batching. The two-RTX-5090 DLO route remains a selected FL2VA-path capacity record, not a live or multi-task-service result.
